Nativity, Theophany, and Meeting of the Lord

Worship and practice · Church year

Nativity, Theophany, and Meeting of the Lord

6 sectionsNot completed
Notes

Nativity, Theophany and the Meeting of the Lord concern Christ’s birth and manifestation in human life. The hymn texts express those events in the language of the Incarnation, while the linked articles identify their biblical and liturgical setting.[1]

What does the Nativity hymn teach?[1]

Nativity means birth; this hymn concerns the birth of Jesus Christ. It describes the star leading those who had worshipped the stars toward recognition of Christ. Its images of light and the Sun of Righteousness present his birth as the revelation of divine wisdom.[1]

Read original passage

Nativity of Christ

Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, hath arisen upon the world as the light of wisdom. For at it, they who worshipped the stars were, by a Star, taught to adore thee, the Sun of Righteousness, and to know thee, the Orient from on high. O Lord, glory to thee.

What does the Theophany hymn reveal about the Trinity?[1]

Theophany means the manifestation of God. The hymn associates Christ’s baptism in the Jordan with the Father’s testimony and the Spirit’s appearance as a dove. Its central teaching is the manifestation of the Trinity at that event.[1]

Read original passage

Theophany

When in Jordan thou wast baptized, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest. For the voice of the Father bare witness unto thee, calling thee his beloved Son, and the Spirit, in the form of a Dove, confirmed the steadfastness of that word: O Christ our God, who didst manifest thyself, and dost enlighten the world, glory to thee.

Who is the elder receiving Christ?[1]

The righteous elder in the hymn is St. Simeon, identified in the Gospel account summarized by the linked OCA article on the Meeting. The hymn addresses Mary as Mother of God and Christ as the Redeemer who grants resurrection. It connects the child received in human arms with the saving identity confessed of him.[1][4]

Read original passage

Meeting of the Lord

Hail, O Virgin Birth-giver of God: for from thee hath shone forth the Sun of Righteousness, Christ our God, who giveth light to those who are in darkness. And rejoice, thou aged, righteous man, that didst receive in thine arms the Redeemer of our souls, who giveth unto us resurrection.

The Nativity in an OCA explanation[2]

The OCA article explains the Nativity as the birth in human life of the eternal Son of God. It describes the feast’s services and their scriptural themes.[2]

Source publication

Nativity of Christ

Open source text

Why is Theophany also called Epiphany?[3]

The OCA article explains Epiphany as manifestation and Theophany as the manifestation of God. Its account places Christ’s baptism and the revelation of Father, Son and Holy Spirit at the centre of the feast.[3]

Source publication

Epiphany

Open source text

What meeting is commemorated?[4]

The OCA article identifies the event as Christ’s presentation in the Jerusalem Temple and his meeting with St. Simeon and the prophetess St. Anna. Their recognition of the child as the promised Christ gives the feast its biblical setting in Luke 2.[4]
